games.name: Fortnite
games.award_evidence: BAFTA's 2019 winners release names Fortnite as the Evolving Game winner.

mechanics.name: Battle Pass
mechanics.detail: Pages of rewards progress through XP earned across Battle Royale, Creative, LEGO Fortnite and Festival experiences.

mechanics.name: Quests
mechanics.detail: Daily, weekly and character quests provide repeatable XP bursts and direct players across modes.

mechanics.name: Persistent live world
mechanics.detail: Epic continually rotates seasons, modes and creator-made experiences inside one account progression layer.

games.return_reason: Documented: cross-mode XP, time-limited passes and recurring quests create a visible near-term loop; the award source also describes Fortnite as an evolving game. Inference: players may return to finish a pass, try a changed island, or meet friends in a new mode.
games.allworld_transfer: Translate seasonal city festivals, creator districts and cross-job quests into one fair pass: contribution XP should work in jobs, homes, civic missions and social events, with badges for completed seasons and public achievements.
games.risk: Pass expiry and heavy content cadence can create FOMO; avoid pay-to-win power and preserve catch-up routes.

games.name: Apex Legends
games.award_evidence: BAFTA's 2020 winners release names Apex Legends as the Multiplayer winner.

mechanics.name: Seasonal Battle Pass
mechanics.detail: Each roughly three-month season brings new Legends, loot and events; Battle Passes award cosmetics, currency and packs through play.

mechanics.name: Challenges
mechanics.detail: Daily and weekly challenges award Stars toward Battle Pass levels, while a free track remains available.

mechanics.name: Ranked competition
mechanics.detail: Ranked Leagues and the ALGS provide skill progression and formal competition using the same game rules.

games.return_reason: Documented: seasonal content, challenge Stars, persistent player level and ranked play supply layered progress. Inference: squads return for both social coordination and the next skill or cosmetic milestone.
games.allworld_transfer: Use role-based city teams, fair matchmaking and seasonal civic leagues; let players earn a shared badge track from work, exploration and cooperative rescue missions rather than combat power.
games.risk: Battle-pass split cadence can pressure completion and monetize status; keep essential city functions permanently available and make rank decay forgiving.

games.name: VALORANT
games.award_evidence: The Esports Awards' 2022 winners page names VALORANT as Esports Game of the Year.

mechanics.name: Acts and Battle Passes
mechanics.detail: Episodes contain Acts, with a new time-bounded Battle Pass each Act and free and premium progression tracks.

mechanics.name: Missions
mechanics.detail: XP from matches and missions advances the Battle Pass and a character contract simultaneously.

mechanics.name: Ranked rating
mechanics.detail: Competitive queues update Ranked Rating and matchmaking; official patch notes document rank and sub-tier adjustments.

games.return_reason: Documented: short Acts, simultaneous mission/contract progress and visible Ranked Rating give each session a measurable target. Inference: players return to improve mastery, preserve team routines and complete an expiring Act track.
games.allworld_transfer: Build fair city leagues where reputation, job mastery and team missions produce visible ratings, with seasonal badges that reward cooperation and transparent contribution rather than hidden power.
games.risk: Rank anxiety and premium cosmetics can narrow participation; provide unranked social spaces, anti-smurf protections and noncompetitive progression.

games.name: Overwatch
games.award_evidence: BAFTA's 2017 winner record names Overwatch as the Multiplayer winner.
games.edition_note: The award and mechanic evidence refer to the original 2016 Overwatch. Overwatch 2-era progression and live-service claims are intentionally excluded.

mechanics.name: Original Competitive Play placements and tiers
mechanics.detail: Blizzard's October 2017 original-Overwatch season page documents placement matches, skill rating and named competitive tiers.

games.return_reason: Historical documented pattern: the original game's placement matches and visible skill tiers gave repeat competitive sessions a legible mastery path. Inference: players could return for rank recovery and social coordination around familiar team roles.
games.allworld_transfer: Historical lesson: use complementary city roles, cooperative objectives and transparent skill tiers without assuming that Overwatch 2's later progression systems belong to the 2017 award winner.
games.risk: The original service was replaced by Overwatch 2, so current sequel systems cannot be used as evidence for the 2017-winning edition.

games.name: League of Legends
games.award_evidence: The Game Awards' 2019 edition archive names League of Legends as Best Esports Game.

mechanics.name: Ranked seasons and rewards
mechanics.detail: Riot documents seasonal rank resets, provisional games and ranked reward missions tied to the climb.

mechanics.name: Seasonal challenges
mechanics.detail: Additional in-game quests and challenges release alongside ranked splits.

mechanics.name: Champion roster and patches
mechanics.detail: Frequent balance patches and a large champion roster continually change viable strategies.

games.return_reason: Documented: ranked splits, missions, patches and champion variety create recurring competitive goals. Inference: players return to learn a changed meta, climb with friends and maintain identity in a long-lived roster.
games.allworld_transfer: Use seasonal job ladders and city missions with role diversity, fair rating and earned badges; rotate scenarios while preserving a player’s long-term civic résumé.
games.risk: Complexity, toxicity and ladder pressure can exclude newcomers; pair AI coaching with strong moderation and low-stakes onboarding.

games.name: Dota 2

award.name: IGN People's Choice Award at gamescom

games.award_evidence: Valve's official Steam page embeds an IGN People's Choice Award gamescom 2011 badge for Dota 2; the organizer archive was unavailable.

mechanics.name: Skill-ranked matchmaking
mechanics.detail: Valve's Glicko update uses Rank and Rank Confidence, with calibration helping returning players regain an accurate placement.

mechanics.name: Hero drafting and mastery
mechanics.detail: Matches begin from a large hero pool and team composition choices, producing different strategic problems each game.

mechanics.name: Replays and competitive ecosystem
mechanics.detail: The official game description and client support persistent multiplayer, co-op and server-side match replays.

games.return_reason: Documented: calibration, Rank Confidence and a large hero pool create a replayable mastery ladder. Inference: players return to test new drafts, improve decision-making and participate in a shared competitive scene.
games.allworld_transfer: Model transparent confidence-based matchmaking for city jobs and missions, where players can try roles without permanent damage and earn durable mastery badges.
games.risk: The award evidence is an official Valve store listing rather than an award organizer archive; onboarding and toxicity remain substantial risks.

games.name: Counter-Strike: Global Offensive
games.award_evidence: The Esports Awards' 2016 archive names Counter-Strike: Global Offensive as Esports Game of the Year.
games.edition_note: The award and mechanics refer to historical CS:GO. Steam app 730 now resolves to Counter-Strike 2 and is not used as evidence for the 2016 edition.

mechanics.name: Historical operations and missions
mechanics.detail: CS:GO's official Operation Shattered Web page documents weekly mission cards, Stars, reward unlocks and an upgradeable Operation Coin.

mechanics.name: Historical round and economy structure
mechanics.detail: Valve's archived CS:GO overview describes objective-based rounds, weapon and armor purchases, in-game economy and Competitive Skill Groups.

mechanics.name: Historical cosmetic collections
mechanics.detail: Operation Shattered Web added weapon collections, agents, stickers and graffiti as operation rewards.

games.return_reason: Historical documented pattern: repeatable rounds, visible skill groups, weekly missions and collectible operation rewards reinforced a skill-first loop in CS:GO. The inference concerns that edition, not Counter-Strike 2.
games.allworld_transfer: Historical lesson: combine short team tasks, durable mastery and non-power identity rewards while keeping the award-era product distinct from its replacement.
games.risk: CS:GO was replaced by Counter-Strike 2, and market-like cosmetics plus high skill gaps remain poor defaults for broad onboarding.

games.name: Rocket League
games.award_evidence: BAFTA's 2017 winner record names Rocket League as the Evolving Game winner.

mechanics.name: Competitive ranks and placements
mechanics.detail: Players complete placement matches, climb skill tiers and can earn rank-specific seasonal rewards and titles.

mechanics.name: Seasonal tournaments
mechanics.detail: Competitive seasons, tournaments and Rocket Pass share a schedule, creating synchronized return windows.

mechanics.name: Challenges and Drops
mechanics.detail: Weekly, season and event challenges award XP, customization items and Drops.

games.return_reason: Documented: tiny matches, clear ranks, scheduled tournaments and challenge drops make progress easy to resume. Inference: players return for mechanical practice, team chemistry and a fresh season reward target.
games.allworld_transfer: Create short cooperative city games and skill trials inside a broader life simulation; reward teamwork and civic achievement with titles, badges and home décor.
games.risk: Rank resets and cosmetic season gates can frustrate occasional players; keep placement fair and rewards attainable after a late start.

games.name: Splatoon
games.award_evidence: The Game Awards' 2015 edition archive names Splatoon as Best Multiplayer Game.

mechanics.name: Turf War
mechanics.detail: Four-versus-four teams compete to cover the arena in ink, with movement and concealment tied to painted territory.

mechanics.name: Gear and ability customization
mechanics.detail: Nintendo's award description documents equipment and gear that change abilities without changing the core objective.

mechanics.name: Splatfests
mechanics.detail: Limited-time themed team events ask players to choose a side and compete for a result.

games.return_reason: Documented: simple Turf War rules, movement options, gear and time-bounded Splatfests combine accessibility with mastery. Inference: people return for quick social matches, event identity and the satisfaction of expressing a playstyle.
games.allworld_transfer: Use approachable city competitions with multiple valid roles, seasonal neighborhood votes and cosmetic identity; keep outcomes legible and avoid pay-gated civic power.
games.risk: Event timing and team imbalance can exclude players; archive past badges and offer practice or late-entry paths.

games.name: Splatoon 3
games.award_evidence: The Japan Game Awards' 2023 organizer page lists Splatoon 3 as an Award for Excellence winner.

mechanics.name: Splatfests and Tricolor Turf War
mechanics.detail: Players vote on one of three themes, then compete in 4v4 and three-team Tricolor battles over a limited event period.

mechanics.name: Seasonal catalog
mechanics.detail: Battles earn points exchanged for seasonal gear, ability chunks, titles, banners and decorations through the catalog.

mechanics.name: Anarchy and Salmon Run
mechanics.detail: Ranked objective modes and four-player co-op wave defense provide distinct repeatable goals.

games.return_reason: Documented: event voting, seasonal catalogs, ranked objectives and co-op waves serve different motivations. Inference: returning is attractive because a player can switch between competitive mastery, social events and collection progress.
games.allworld_transfer: Mirror this with city elections, cooperative disaster response, job skill ladders and seasonal civic catalogs, awarding badges for contribution across modes.
games.risk: Multiple currencies and event rules can overwhelm; keep the primary social loop clear and make old cosmetics and achievements recoverable.

games.name: Destiny
games.award_evidence: AIAS's 18th D.I.C.E. winners page names Destiny for Outstanding Achievement in Online Gameplay.
games.edition_note: This is Destiny 1, now under Bungie's legacy support. It no longer receives planned game updates or content.

mechanics.name: Weekly reward lockouts
mechanics.detail: Bungie support documents weekly Nightfall, raid, challenge and playlist rewards, with checkpoints and character-based reset rules.

mechanics.name: Raids and challenges
mechanics.detail: Raids are end-game co-op activities with progression checkpoints, hard modes and separate challenge rewards.

mechanics.name: Crucible and strikes
mechanics.detail: Matchmade PvE strikes and PvP Crucible playlists provide repeatable social and competitive activities.

games.return_reason: Historical/legacy pattern: weekly resets, raid checkpoints and shared activities created a calendar of goals. Bungie's support page documents the remaining legacy activities, not a currently evolving service.
games.allworld_transfer: Historical lesson: cooperative checkpoints and durable professional badges can create team rituals, but weekly lockouts should not erase a citizen's core history or require current-service assumptions.
games.risk: Bungie states that Destiny 1 receives no planned game updates or content; treat its loop as legacy evidence and avoid coercive lockouts.

games.name: Destiny 2
games.award_evidence: The Game Awards' 2019 edition archive names Destiny 2 as Best Community Support.

mechanics.name: Seasonal challenges
mechanics.detail: Weekly challenge sets target seasonal content and rituals, award XP and rewards, and remain completable until season end.

mechanics.name: Guardian Ranks and commendations
mechanics.detail: Guardian Ranks showcase knowledge and skill; elite ranks require commendations from fellow players.

mechanics.name: Weekly ritual reset
mechanics.detail: Bounties, raid challenges, Nightfalls, Trials and powerful rewards reset weekly.

games.return_reason: Documented: seasonal challenges, weekly resets, ranks and commendations combine self-improvement with community recognition. Inference: players return to keep a fireteam routine, complete a title path or chase a better build.
games.allworld_transfer: Use commendations from real human teammates, explainable AI assistance and weekly civic missions that build a public trust record without letting popularity buy power.
games.risk: As of 2026 Bungie says planned live-service updates ended; transfer the durable badge/rank model without copying content churn or sunset anxiety.

games.name: Final Fantasy XIV
games.award_evidence: BAFTA's Evolving Game archive marks Final Fantasy XIV Online as the 2023 winner.

mechanics.name: Weekly Challenge Log
mechanics.detail: The official manual lists challenges with progress and rewards; progress resets weekly.

mechanics.name: Duty Roulette
mechanics.detail: Daily and duty roulettes match players into dungeons, trials and raids with reward bonuses and role incentives.

mechanics.name: Achievements and titles
mechanics.detail: The Lodestone database exposes thousands of achievements with title, equipment and point rewards.

games.return_reason: Documented: a persistent world layers weekly challenges, daily group duties, crafting and achievement titles. Inference: players return for routine social obligations, story continuation and a character identity that accumulates over years.
games.allworld_transfer: Prioritize a durable civic identity: jobs, homes, clubs and city achievements should coexist with weekly cooperative duties and titles that reflect helpful human behavior.
games.risk: MMO breadth and time demands can overwhelm; support catch-up, asynchronous contributions and clear onboarding for returning residents.

games.name: World of Warcraft

award.name: D.I.C.E. Awards
award.category: Massively Multiplayer/Persistent World Game of the Year

games.award_evidence: AIAS's 2005 award page names World of Warcraft as Massively Multiplayer/Persistent World Game of the Year.

mechanics.name: Persistent character progression
mechanics.detail: AIAS describes Azeroth as a persistent online RPG built around exploration, quests and challenges.

mechanics.name: Seasonal endgame cycles
mechanics.detail: Raids, Mythic+ and rotating seasons provide repeatable high-skill group content and achievement targets.

mechanics.name: Guild social progression
mechanics.detail: Guilds coordinate players for group content, shared goals and social identity in the persistent world.

games.return_reason: Documented: quests, exploration and a persistent world are the foundation; current endgame adds rotating group challenges. Inference: returning players reconnect with guilds, continue a character story and pursue mastery or prestige goals.
games.allworld_transfer: Treat Allworld cities as persistent places where residents build work histories, homes, relationships and public badges, with optional guild-like crews and humane catch-up.
games.risk: Long subscription-style obligation and legacy complexity can exclude people with limited time; support episodic participation and transparent AI help.

games.name: Sea of Thieves
games.award_evidence: BAFTA's Evolving Game archive marks Sea of Thieves as the 2021 winner.

mechanics.name: Guilds
mechanics.detail: Up to 24 pirates can join a Guild, sail on friends' pledged ships while offline and raise shared Guild Reputation for rewards.

mechanics.name: Voyages and world events
mechanics.detail: Crews choose Trading Company voyages, Tall Tales or world events; Season 11 added direct launch and on-demand Raid Voyages.

mechanics.name: Milestones and Commendations
mechanics.detail: Captaincy tracks long-term playstyle milestones, while seasonal commendations and Renown unlock cosmetics.

games.return_reason: Documented: emergent voyages, shared Guild reputation, long-term milestones and cosmetic commendations reward both planned and improvised play. Inference: humans return for crew stories, status and a world that can surprise them.
games.allworld_transfer: Make human crews, neighborhoods and guilds central, with shared reputation for reliable work, public service and memorable stories; fair AI can fill gaps without replacing human agency.
games.risk: Emergent PvP and loss can feel hostile; preserve safe social spaces and explain risk/reward clearly.

games.name: Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege

award.name: Game Critics Awards: Best of E3 2014

games.award_evidence: The Game Critics Awards' Best of E3 2014 page names Rainbow Six Siege as Best PC Game; this was pre-release showcase recognition.

mechanics.name: Ranked seasons and rewards
mechanics.detail: Ranked 3.0 adds placement matches, rank progression and a Competitive Rewards track each season.

mechanics.name: Reputation and commendations
mechanics.detail: Players can commend teammates for valor, dedication and guidance; consistent commendations activate a visible streak and pack bonus.

mechanics.name: Long-term badges
mechanics.detail: Ubisoft tracks rank and reputation and awards badges for challenge completion displayed on an Operator card.

games.return_reason: Documented: destructible tactical play, seasonal ranks, reputation feedback and visible badges create both team and individual progress. Inference: players return to refine map knowledge, maintain squad trust and prove improvement.
games.allworld_transfer: Use explainable reputation, human commendations and role-specific city missions; reward reliable cooperation with badges while keeping AI fair, auditable and subordinate to player choice.
games.risk: Toxicity, smurfing and punitive reputation systems can harm newcomers; provide appeals, practice spaces and nonzero-sum social roles.
